title: serving-runtime-team-wiki-playbook-2027-12-01
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical team wiki and playbook for the Serving Runtime at Redwood Inference. It consolidates the runtime architecture, kernel scheduling guidance, profiling playbooks, benchmarking suite, release notes for the December 2027 cycle, known issues, operational runbooks, and onboarding steps for new engineers. Use this as the single source of truth for architecture decisions, perf troubleshooting, and release-to-run operations.

1. Runtime architecture (high-level)

Intro: The Serving Runtime is organized as a set of cooperating services designed for high-throughput, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Primary components: 

- runtime-core: model loading, KV cache management, execution graph
- kernel-scheduler: selects kernels/strategy per op and dispatches to device queues
- batcher: continuous batching layer (adaptive per-tenant policies)
- routing: policy-based request routing and fallback logic
- cache-service: prefix/KV cache with hot-key eviction and lifecycle API
- telemetry-agent: streaming metrics/traces to Redwood observability

Principles: 
- Keep the hot path minimal: critical path executes in runtime-core and kernel-scheduler only.
- Deterministic scheduling heuristics where possible; fallback randomization for burst isolation.
- Observability at token granularity for SLO analysis.

Architecture diagram (textual):
runtime-proxy -> batcher -> runtime-core -> kernel-scheduler -> GPU-device-queues
cache-service <-> runtime-core (KV/cache lookup and population)
telemetry-agent emits: token_latency_ms, kernel_miss_rate, batch_size_distribution

2. Kernel scheduling: policy & configuration

Goals: minimize tail latency while maintaining high throughput and kernel utilization.

Key concepts:
- Kernel variant: quantized vs. fp16 path, fused attention vs unfused
- Scheduling domain: per-model, per-device-type (A100/H100/L4), per-tenancy class
- Weight residency: hot/cold model categorization to pre-warm kernels

Default policies (implemented in kernel-scheduler v2.3):
- Latency-first: for requests with priority>=90 use single-request fast-path (no batching) with optimized kernels.
- Throughput-first: for background/low-priority requests allow unbounded batching up to 128 tokens or 64 requests (configurable).
- Mixed: adaptive windowing: if 95th percentile latency for tenant > configured SLO, shrink batch window by 25% for next minute.

Config example (YAML):
kernel_scheduler:
  device_profiles:
    - name: h100-80gb
      preferred_kernels: [fused_attention_fp16, matmul_int8]
      warm_residency_threshold: 10m
  policies:
    latency_first:
      priority_threshold: 90
      max_batch: 1
    throughput_first:
      max_batch: 64
      max_tokens: 128
    adaptive_windowing:
      initial_window_ms: 12
      shrink_factor: 0.75

Operational knobs to tune under incidents: 
- max_batch (reduce to lower tail latency)
- kernel_variant_preference (force fused or legacy if regressions observed)
- warm_residency_threshold (shorten to keep weights resident for hot models)

3. Profiling playbook (how to collect and interpret data)

When to profile: new model onboarding, performance regression alerts, new kernel releases, tenant complaints about latency.

Step-by-step:
1) Reproduce traffic pattern in staging using perf-bench harness (see Benchmarking Suite).
2) Enable sampling profiler on target runtime instance: `sudo /opt/runtime/bin/prof-agent --sample 100ms --duration 2m --out /tmp/profile.pb`
3) Capture kernel-level counters from kernel-scheduler: `curl -s http://localhost:9102/metrics?type=kernel`
4) Collect device-side traces (NVIDIA Nsight-like): `nvprof --trace-modes=all --output device.trace` (private deployments may use platform-specific tooling).
5) Aggregate telemetry: `rdw telemetry export --start 2027-12-10T10:00Z --end 2027-12-10T10:02Z --metrics token_latency_ms,kernel_miss_rate`

Interpreting outputs:
- High kernel_miss_rate -> scheduler choosing suboptimal kernels or missing cached kernel candidates. Check kernel table `GET /admin/kernel-table` for fallback history.
- Small batch_size distribution with high device utilization -> batching window too small; increase initial_window_ms.
- Long tail attributable to cold model loads -> increase warm_residency_threshold or pre-warm weights during rollout.

Recommended profiling checklist (short):
- Confirm baseline on staging (date/version)
- Record exact model commit hash and quantization profile
- Capture 95th/99th percentiles, not only median
- Attach traces to ticket with run ID and links to telemetry exports

4. Benchmarking suite (perf-bench)

Purpose: reproduce production-like workload, measure tokens/sec, tokens/ms, p99 latency, kernel utilization.

Components:
- perf-bench runner (k8s job) that can replay request traces or generate synthetic prompt distributions.
- workload profiles: chat-short, chat-long, completion-long, embedding-bulk
- metrics collector that pushes to a local influx instance for trend analysis

Example perf-bench command: 
perf-bench run --profile chat-long --concurrency 200 --duration 600s --target http://staging-runtime:8080/generate --out /tmp/bench-20271201.json

Benchmark table (example):
| profile | concurrency | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | tokens/s |
| chat-short | 200 | 30 | 120 | 240 | 35k |
| chat-long | 100 | 80 | 350 | 720 | 12k |
| embedding-bulk | 500 | 12 | 40 | 90 | 80k |

Best practices: run before every release on a representative device fleet, and compare against previous baseline. Store results in `/perf-bench/archive/YYYY-MM-DD/`.

5. Release notes — v2027.12.0 (summary)

Highlights:
- kernel-scheduler v2.3: adaptive windowing added; default latency-first policy adjusted for multi-tenant workloads.
- runtime-core: faster KV cache eviction path; 18% median token latency improvement for short-chat profile.
- perf-bench: added chat-long workload and improved trace replay fidelity.

Migration notes:
- Default adaptive_windowing.initial_window_ms changed from 20ms -> 12ms. Traffic teams should validate tenant SLOs after upgrade.
- Deprecated kernel flag `--prefer-legacy-attention` (scheduled removal in v2028.03). If you rely on legacy kernels, pin scheduler policy.

Rollback plan:
1) Switch kernel-scheduler to previous stable image tag: `kubectl set image deploy/kernel-scheduler kernel-scheduler=redwood/kernel-scheduler:v2.2.9`
2) Revert runtime-core config map to previous: `kubectl apply -f runtime-config-v2.2.9.yaml`
3) Restart batcher pods one zone at a time to avoid cascading cold starts.

6. Known issues (current)

- ISSUE-2310: H100 driver regression (nv-drv-2027.11.5) causes occasional kernel compile failures leading to 500s for quantized paths. Workaround: pin driver to nv-drv-2027.10.2 and restart node. Status: in_progress.
- ISSUE-2444: Large embedding-bulk workloads trigger memory spikes in cache-service when concurrent warm-ups exceed 200; mitigation: throttle pre-warm concurrency to 50. Status: monitoring.
- ISSUE-2122: p99 spike for chat-short after kernel-scheduler adaptive shrink; root cause under investigation (related to tenancy burst windows). Status: triaged.

7. Runtime runbooks (operational procedures)

A) High p99 latency alert (runbook):
1. Pager triggers for p99_token_latency > 500ms for 5m.
2. Check telemetry dash: token_latency_ms, batch_size_distribution, kernel_miss_rate.
3. If kernel_miss_rate > 1% escalate to runtime-oncall to review kernel-table; run `rdw admin kernel-table`
4. Temporarily switch tenants with critical SLOs to latency_first policy: `rdw admin set-policy --tenant <TENANT> --policy latency_first`
5. If issue persists, roll back kernel-scheduler to v2.2.9 (see rollback plan).
6. Document findings and link profiling traces to postmortem ticket.

B) Model cold-start storm:
1. Identify affected model using telemetry trace ids and request patterns.
2. Throttle pre-warm operations: `rdw cache prewarm --concurrency 20`
3. Scale runtime-core pods with warm-residency-friendly placement: `kubectl scale deploy/runtime-core --replicas 10`
4. Schedule follow-up: increase warm_residency_threshold for critical models.

8. Team wiki & onboarding (quickstart for new engineers)

First week checklist: 
- Read this playbook and serving-runtime-architecture-playbook.
- Run perf-bench locally against staging (see Benchmarking Suite) and produce a baseline report.
- Shadow an oncall rotation and observe 1 pager handling session.
- Complete profiling lab: collect a 2m sampling profile and produce a short summary (attach to PR).

Useful commands and snippets (appendix):
- Start profiler: `sudo /opt/runtime/bin/prof-agent --sample 100ms --duration 2m --out /tmp/profile.pb`
- Export telemetry: `rdw telemetry export --start $START --end $END --metrics token_latency_ms,kernel_miss_rate`
- Kernel table: `curl -s http://localhost:8081/admin/kernel-table | jq '.'`
- Perf-bench: `perf-bench run --profile chat-short --concurrency 200 --target http://staging-runtime:8080/generate`
